subject: southern cassowary
title: A Bird With a 12 cm Dagger on Each Foot Has Killed Two People

scenes.text: The most dangerous bird on Earth can't even fly.
The southern cassowary of Australia and New Guinea stands up to 1.8 metres tall. A big female weighs around 58 kilograms, as much as an adult human.
On each foot, the inner toe carries a claw up to 12 centimetres long, shaped like a dagger. It kicks forward with both feet and jumps nearly two metres.
It runs at 50 kilometres an hour through thick jungle. One study counted 221 attacks, 150 of them on people.
In 1926, a teenager in Queensland died from a kick to the neck. In 2019, a Florida man who bred them fell near one, and it killed him.
Two human deaths in a century, from a bird that mostly eats fruit. Its weapon isn't the beak. It's the foot.

description:
The southern cassowary carries a dagger-shaped claw up to 12 centimetres long on the inner toe of each foot, and it has killed two people since 1900.
It stands up to 1.8 metres tall, big females weigh around 58 kilograms, it runs at 50 kilometres an hour, jumps nearly two metres and swims rivers. A study of 221 attacks found 150 on humans; the recorded human deaths were a 16-year-old in Queensland in 1926 and a Florida breeder in 2019, both from kicks.
Which bird do you think is more dangerous, the cassowary or the ostrich?
first_comment: Cassowaries swallow rainforest fruit whole and spread the seeds, so whole forests depend on the bird with the dagger. Which dangerous animal should we rank next?
